Overview



## What is NVIDIA Omniverse?

NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries, part of NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, provides prebuilt capabilities for building simulation-ready worlds that [physical AI](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/generative-physical-ai/) teams can use to train, test, and validate systems before real-world deployment. Developers can integrate libraries, APIs, and services for OpenUSD data interoperability, rendering, physics, sensor simulation, validation, and runtime workflows into existing applications, where AI agents can use them as tools to build those worlds faster.

### NVIDIA Omniverse Libraries Give AI Agents Tools to Build Physical AI Applications

See how Omniverse libraries bring NVIDIA RTX™ rendering, sensor simulation, and GPU-accelerated physics into agent-ready workflows for physical and industrial AI.

[Read the Announcement](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-agent-toolkit-expands-with-new-omniverse-libraries-putting-ai-agents-to-work-building-simulation-ready-worlds)


Technology



## Core Omniverse Libraries and Services

Use Omniverse libraries and services to add physical AI simulation capabilities into applications, tools, and agent-ready workflows.

![OpenUSD](https://www.nvidia.com/content/nvidiaGDC/us/en_US/omniverse/home/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/nv_container_2397652/nv_container/nv_container/nv_image_copy.coreimg.svg/1784562313950/m48-usd-composer.svg)

### OpenUSD Data and Interoperability

Connect, organize, and exchange 3D scene data across applications and simulation pipelines.

- **Use it when**: You need durable scene structure, asset handoff, or application interoperability.
- **Agent-ready role**: Agents can inspect, organize, convert, and route scene data.

[Explore OpenUSD](https://developer.nvidia.com/openusd?size=n_6_n&sort-field=featured&sort-direction=desc)

![NVIDIA RTX](https://www.nvidia.com/content/nvidiaGDC/us/en_US/omniverse/home/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/nv_container_2397652/nv_container/nv_container_1303210201/nv_image_copy.coreimg.svg/1784562314028/m48-sample-scenes.svg)

### RTX Rendering and Simulation

Preview scenes, generate sensor outputs, and produce visual evidence from simulation-ready worlds.

- **Use it when**: You need visual preflight, synthetic sensor output, or simulation-ready scene review.
- **Agent-ready role**: Agents can trigger renders, simulate sensors, and return visual evidence.

[Explore ovrtx Library](https://github.com/nvidia-omniverse/ovrtx)

[View ovrtx Examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovrtx/tree/main/examples)

![NVIDIA PhysX](https://www.nvidia.com/content/nvidiaGDC/us/en_US/omniverse/home/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/nv_container_2397652/nv_container/nv_container_1923310725/nv_image_copy.coreimg.svg/1784562314103/m48-physics-physx.svg)

### Physics Simulation

Simulate motion, contacts, and physically grounded behavior for robotics and digital twin workflows.

- **Use it when**: You need to test collisions, motion, dynamics, or physics readiness.
- **Agent-ready role**: Agents can run physics-readiness checks and route issues for review.

[Explore ovphysx Library](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/PhysX/tree/main/ovphysx)

[Learn About Newton Physics](https://developer.nvidia.com/newton-physics)

![Explore SimReady](https://www.nvidia.com/content/nvidiaGDC/us/en_US/omniverse/home/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/nv_container_2397652/nv_container/nv_container_copy/nv_image_copy.coreimg.svg/1784562314170/m48-textures.svg)

### Simulation-Ready Asset Validation

Check OpenUSD assets against simulation-ready requirements before downstream training, testing, or deployment.

- **Use it when**: You need acceptance gates before moving assets into physical AI simulation workflows.
- **Agent-ready role**: Agents can run validation checks and return pass/fail evidence.


[Explore SimReady](https://github.com/NVIDIA/simready-foundation)


Starting Options



## Choose How to Build With Omniverse

Start with libraries, agent-ready tools, blueprints, or sample workflows, based on what you want to build.

### Build With Libraries

Use Omniverse libraries when you need agent-ready tools for rendering, physics, sensor simulation, OpenUSD operations, or validation in an application or service.

**Best for**: Developers building custom tools, plugins, services, or physical AI workflows.

[Explore Libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse)

### Use Agent Skills

Use Omniverse Agent Skills when you want AI agents to call Omniverse tools for scene inspection, rendering, simulation, validation, or review tasks.

**Best for**: Teams building agent-assisted workflows with human review.

[Explore Agent Skills](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills)

### Start From Blueprints

Use blueprints when you want a reference architecture or workflow that shows how Omniverse libraries and agent skills fit together.

**Best for:** Teams moving from concept to implementation without starting from scratch.

[View Blueprints](https://build.nvidia.com/explore/simulation)

### Explore Samples and Labs

Try experimental samples, integration patterns, and proof-of-concept apps that show how Omniverse libraries can be used in real workflows.

**Best fo** r: Developers evaluating early patterns before building their own integration.

[Explore Omniverse Labs](https://nvidia-omniverse.github.io/omniverse-labs/)


Use Cases

Agility, Apptronik, Fourier Intelligence, Unitree

### Synthetic Data Generation

Generate physically grounded synthetic data from simulation-ready worlds to train and test physical AI models.

[Explore Synthetic Data Generation](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/use-cases/synthetic-data-physical-ai/)

![Use synthetic data to save time and money](https://www.nvidia.com/content/nvidiaGDC/us/en_US/omniverse/home/_jcr_content/root/responsivegrid/nv_container_1078396056/nv_tabs/item_2/nv_image_copy_copy.coreimg.100.1290.jpeg/1784562315283/nvidia-omniverse-synthetic-data-generation.jpeg)

### Autonomous Vehicle Simulation

Prepare simulation-ready environments for testing perception systems, sensors, and autonomous vehicle scenarios.

- Structure road, facility, and scenario data with sensor-ready OpenUSD assets.
- Simulate cameras, lidar, radar, and visual preflight for perception workflows.

  "markdown": "Industrial Ecosystem Adopts Mega NVIDIA Omniverse Blueprint to Train Physical AI in Digital Twins \| NVIDIA Blog![country_code](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/1x1-00000000.png)

[Skip to content](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/mega-omniverse-blueprint-industrial-digital-twins/#primary)

Advances in physical AI are enabling organizations to embrace [embodied AI](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/embodied-ai/) across their operations, bringing unprecedented intelligence, automation and productivity to the world’s factories, warehouses and industrial facilities.

[Humanoid robots](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/use-cases/humanoid-robots/) can work alongside human teams, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) can navigate complex warehouse environments, and intelligent cameras and visual AI agents can monitor and optimize entire facilities. In these ways, [physical AI](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/generative-physical-ai/) is becoming integral to today’s industrial operations.

Helping industrial enterprises accelerate the development, testing and deployment of physical AI, the [Mega NVIDIA Omniverse Blueprint](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/mega-multi-robot-fleets-for-industrial-automation) for testing multi-robot fleets in [digital twins](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/digital-twin/) is now available in preview on [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/mega-multi-robot-fleets-for-industrial-automation).

At [Hannover Messe](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/events/hannover-messe/) — a trade show on industrial development running through April 4 in Germany — manufacturing, warehousing and supply chain leaders such as [Accenture and Schaeffler](https://newsroom.accenture.com/news/2025/accenture-and-schaeffler-pave-the-way-for-industrial-humanoid-robots-with-nvidia-and-microsoft-technologies) are showcasing their adoption of the blueprint to simulate Digit, a humanoid robot from Agility Robotics, and discussing how they use [industrial AI](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/industrial-ai/) and digital twins to optimize facility layouts, material flow and collaboration between humans and robots inside complex production environments.

In addition, NVIDIA ecosystem partners — including [Delta Electronics](https://www.delta-emea.com/en-gb/news/delta-demonstrates-how-its-ai-enabled-solutions-foster-intelligent-industries-and-sustainable-energy-transition-at-hannover-messe-2025), [Rockwell Automation](https://www.rockwellautomation.com/en-nl/company/news/press-releases/emulate3d-factory-test-to-launch-at-hannover-messe-2025.html) and [Siemens](https://press.siemens.com/global/en/pressrelease/siemens-accelerates-path-toward-ai-driven-industries-through-innovation-and) — are announcing further integrations with [NVIDIA Omniverse](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) and [NVIDIA AI](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/ai/) technologies at the event.

## **Digital Twins — the Training Ground for Physical AI**

[Industrial facility digital twins](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/use-cases/industrial-facility-digital-twins/) are physically accurate virtual replicas of real-world facilities that serve as critical testing grounds for simulating and validating physical AI and how robots and autonomous fleets interact, collaborate and tackle complex tasks before  deployment.

Developers can use [NVIDIA Omniverse](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse) platform technologies and the Universal Scene Description ( [OpenUSD](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/usd/)) framework to develop digital twins of their facilities and processes. This simulation-first approach dramatically accelerates development cycles while reducing the costs and risks associated with real-world testing.

## **Built for a Diversity of Robots and AI Agents**

The Mega blueprint equips industrial enterprises with a reference workflow for combining [sensor simulation](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/sensor-simulation/) and [synthetic data generation](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/what-is-synthetic-data/) to simulate complex human-robot interactions and verify the performance of autonomous systems in industrial digital twins.

Enterprises can use Mega to test various robot brains and policies at scale for mobility, navigation, dexterity and spatial reasoning. This enables fleets comprising different types of robots to work together as a coordinated system.

As robot brains execute their missions in simulation, they perceive the results of their actions through sensor simulation and plan their next action. This cycle continues until the policies are refined and ready for deployment.

Once validated, these policies are deployed to real robots, which continue to learn from their environment — sending sensor information back through the entire loop and creating a continuous learning and improvement cycle.

YouTube

## **Transforming Industrial Operations With Visual AI Agents**

In addition to AMRs and humanoid robots, advanced visual AI agents extract information from live and recorded video data, enabling new levels of intelligence and automation. These visual AI agents bring real-time contextual awareness to robots and help to improve worker safety, maintain warehouse compliance, support visual inspection and maximize space utilization.

To support developers building visual AI agents, which can be integrated with the Mega blueprint, NVIDIA last year announced an [AI Blueprint for video search and summarization](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/video-search-and-summarization) (VSS). At Hannover Messe, leading partners are featuring how they use the VSS blueprint to improve productivity and operational efficiency.

## **Accelerating Industrial Digitalization**

The industrial world is now experiencing its software-defined moment, with visual AI agents and digital twins as the training ground for physical AI.

[Join NVIDIA and its partners at Hannover Messe](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/events/hannover-messe/) to discover how AI agents and real-time simulation, powered by [NVIDIA’s Three Computer Solution](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/three-computers-robotics/), are reshaping [industrial](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/industries/industrial-sector/) workflows and driving innovation, automation and efficiency in [manufacturing](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/industries/manufacturing/).

[_Read the technical blog_](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/simulating-robots-in-industrial-facility-digital-twins/) _to learn more about the Mega blueprint for industrial robot fleets._ _See the blueprint in action on this_ [_interactive demo page_](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/mega-multi-robot-fleets-for-industrial-automation).

_Stay up to date by subscribing to_ [_NVIDIA news_](https://nvda.ws/3u5KPv1) _, joining the Omniverse_ [_community_](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse/community) _and following NVIDIA Omniverse on_ [_Instagram_](https://www.instagram.com/nvidiaomniverse/) _,_ [_LinkedIn_](https://www.linkedin.com/showcase/nvidia-omniverse/) _,_ [_Medium_](https://medium.com/@nvidiaomniverse) _and_ [_X_](https://twitter.com/nvidiaomniverse) _._

_Explore the new self-paced_ [_Learn OpenUSD_](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/learn/learning-path/openusd/) _training curriculum that includes free NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute courses for 3D practitioners and developers._

  "markdown": "# Visualizing an iTwin

## [Why visualization?](https://developer.bentley.com/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/\#why-visualization)

Visualization in digital twins is all about bringing assets to life, which is exactly the purpose of iTwins. The power of iTwin visualization lies in their ability to combine data from various repositories—both internal and external—and present it in a unified, rich context. Imagine being able to visualize sensor data, design elements, and real-world conditions all at once. This not only creates a holistic representation of the asset but also enables dynamic interactions with asset data. From real-time operational monitoring to detailed project reviews, the possibilities are vast and adaptable to many infrastructure domains.

## [Key scenarios](https://developer.bentley.com/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/\#key-scenarios)

### [Visualizing IoT sensor data](https://developer.bentley.com/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/\#visualizing-iot-sensor-data)

One of the most frequently requested features of the iTwin Platform is their ability to visualize real-time sensor data. This functionality is essential during the operational phase of assets and is also valuable for ongoing design efforts. It allows users to overlay real-time environmental data—such as temperature, occupancy, and other metrics—directly onto the model's elements.

![Example 1 - An iTwin of a wind farm displaying real-time sensor data of a turbine.](https://developer.bentley.com/images/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/example-windfarm-iot.png)Example 1 - An iTwin of a wind farm displaying real-time sensor data of a turbine.

### [Visual overlays and markers](https://developer.bentley.com/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/\#visual-overlays-and-markers)

The iTwin Platform offers a variety of visual overlays, including decorators, markers, and annotations, which allow users to enhance their models in numerous ways. These tools are useful for highlighting key areas, visualizing workflows, and incorporating contextual information from external sources like maps or documents.

![Example 2 - Markers visualizing smart devices inside a house model.](https://developer.bentley.com/images/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/example-smart-house.png)Example 2 - Markers visualizing smart devices inside a house model.

### [Interactive iTwin experiences](https://developer.bentley.com/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/\#interactive-itwin-experiences)

The iTwin Platform goes beyond passive viewing by empowering users to directly interact with the iTwin. This interaction can include fetching element information or creating dynamic tools that extend functionality. By integrating these tools, iTwin applications can deliver custom experiences tailored to specific industry requirements.

![Example 3 - An interactive tool for sectioning out design models using clipping planes.](https://developer.bentley.com/images/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/example-clipping-planes.png)Example 3 - An interactive tool for sectioning out design models using clipping planes.

![Example 4 - A camera tool for visualizing an iTwin from multiple perspectives.](https://developer.bentley.com/images/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/example-camera-tool.png)Example 4 - A camera tool for visualizing an iTwin from multiple perspectives.

### [Advanced visualization techniques](https://developer.bentley.com/use-cases/visualizing-an-itwin/\#advanced-visualization-techniques)

Beyond standard visualization, the iTwin Platform supports advanced techniques such as animations, particle effects, markup tools, heat maps, and more. These features allow users to augment visualization, emphasize important data, or even create animated sequences to simulate real-world scenarios.

Visualization isn't just about seeing—it's about experiencing your data in new, innovative ways.
